original_question: Determine the Frobenius variety generated by the symmetric numerical semigroups.
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("Frobenius Varieties"), final unnumbered open question: "What is the Frobenius variety generated only by the symmetric ones?" ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft points to the correct open problem in Section 4 and correctly isolates the symmetric half of the paper’s paired question about symmetric versus pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups. It also keeps the focus on Frobenius varieties rather than drifting to neighboring questions about quotients, Toms decompositions, or maximal embedding dimension. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
missing_details: You should specify that the family consists of all symmetric numerical semigroups, not an arbitrary chosen subclass. The paper asks for the variety generated "only by the symmetric ones." ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

You need the paper’s definition of a Frobenius variety: a nonempty family 𝒱 of numerical semigroups such that if S,T ∈ 𝒱, then S ∩ T ∈ 𝒱, and if S ∈ 𝒱 with S ≠ ℕ, then S ∪ {F(S)} ∈ 𝒱. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

You should define what “generated by” means here: the Frobenius variety generated by a family 𝔽 is the intersection of all Frobenius varieties containing 𝔽. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, define a numerical semigroup as a cofinite submonoid of ℕ = {0,1,2,…}, and define F(S) as the Frobenius number of S. These ambient conventions are assumed throughout the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1304.6552))
You should define “symmetric numerical semigroup” in the paper’s sense: S is symmetric if x ∉ S implies F(S) − x ∈ S. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

The paper frames this question after observing that the Frobenius variety generated by irreducible numerical semigroups is the whole class of numerical semigroups, with irreducible semigroups being exactly the symmetric or pseudo-symmetric ones; this context explains why the symmetric-only problem is the sharpened target. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
refined_question: Let Sym be the family of all symmetric numerical semigroups S ⊆ ℕ, where ℕ = {0,1,2,…}, F(S) denotes the Frobenius number of S, and S is called symmetric if for every integer x, x ∉ S implies F(S) − x ∈ S. Determine the least Frobenius variety containing Sym; equivalently, determine the family ⋂{𝒱 : 𝒱 is a Frobenius variety and Sym ⊆ 𝒱}, where a Frobenius variety is a nonempty family 𝒱 of numerical semigroups such that (i) if S,T ∈ 𝒱, then S ∩ T ∈ 𝒱, and (ii) if S ∈ 𝒱 and S ≠ ℕ, then S ∪ {F(S)} ∈ 𝒱. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s wording, but it is not fully stand-alone because the paper first defines Frobenius varieties and the notion of the variety generated by a family, and only then poses the symmetric-only question. The nearby context also supplies the definition of symmetry and explains the surrounding hierarchy: irreducible numerical semigroups are exactly the symmetric or pseudo-symmetric ones, and the Frobenius variety generated by all irreducible numerical semigroups is the whole class of numerical semigroups. That makes the exact paper-faithful target the least Frobenius variety containing every symmetric numerical semigroup, with no further broadening. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
